sections.content: How many people are "advertising accounts managers and creative directors"?

47,535 people

were counted on the census as "advertising accounts managers and creative directors" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Advertising accounts managers and creative directors plan, design, and direct the advertising activities of an organisation.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "advertising accounts managers and creative directors", 18.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "advertising accounts managers and creative directors" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "advertising accounts managers and creative directors" included:

  • primary education teaching professionals
  • marketing and commercial managers
  • speech and language therapists

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "advertising accounts managers and creative directors" there were a similar number of men and women (50.6% compared with 49.4%).

This means "advertising accounts managers and creative directors" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 50.6% and women made up 49.4% of "advertising accounts managers and creative directors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "advertising accounts managers and creative directors" included:

  • police community support officers
  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "advertising accounts managers and creative directors" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "advertising accounts managers and creative directors" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "advertising accounts managers and creative directors", 6.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (84.9% compared with 15.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (77.4%) than self-employed (22.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Hackney, this is in the same region of London.
